node_definition.done_when: A test in tests/test_one_call_explains_any_ref.py builds a fixture where section A waits on B, B is held by a running run, and a followup on A is open; read_plan(view="why", section="A") names the wait on B with its kind, B's run and its held path, and the followup, inside the read's size contract. A ref that does not resolve is refused with the nearest refs that do. The composition lives in a new module, reckon/why_view.py, reading the existing owners (the roadmap's section edges, the live run partition and the plan's events) rather than re-deriving them; no new MCP tool and no CLI verb is added. On the base commit the view is refused as unknown and the test fails there. The negative control is executed and logged. Gate: tests/test_one_call_explains_any_ref.py tests/test_mcp_tools.py. baseline_suite and after_suite are run with the project's armed suite command, PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/test_one_call_explains_any_ref.py, at the base and at the head, each log naming its revision, tree and literal command and ending EXIT=. Every test file that imports a production module the node changed adds no failure against a base arm: run both arms from git archive extractions on node-local disk with the main checkout's .env linked, record both logs, and re-run any id that differs between arms serially three times on each revision. ruff check and ruff format --check add no findings on the staged paths. Run the gate in the foreground on the fleet allocation.
